scope: Concurrent Wan-Animate-2 Hand2Dex smoke orchestration and recovery
summary: The first concurrent pair exposed a fixed distributed rendezvous port; the first fix omitted RANK/WORLD_SIZE; later A800-4 retries correctly failed preflight after another job occupied the GPUs; A800-1 then exposed a stale shared Triton cache. The runner now isolates ports, rank variables, and compiler caches per experiment.
evidence: Case 1 seed 42 completed on A800-4 while the simultaneous case 2 run failed with NCCL remote-process errors on the shared default port 12345.
Port-isolated retries recorded distinct ports 15001 and 15203 but failed with KeyError RANK because upstream initialization skipped its defaults once MASTER_ADDR was set.
After RANK=0 and WORLD_SIZE=1 were added, A800-4 retries failed closed before launch because another authorized workload reduced free memory below 61,000 MiB.
A800-1 retries used distinct ports and complete rank variables but failed in torch Inductor with a PY_SSIZE_T_CLEAN error from the shared Triton cache.
The current runner records experiment-owned TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR and TRITON_CACHE_DIR in addition to CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and rendezvous settings.
lessons: Concurrent multi-GPU jobs require unique rendezvous ports even when physical GPU sets are disjoint.
Setting MASTER_ADDR explicitly also requires the upstream machine-rank variables.
Compiler caches are environment-sensitive experiment inputs and must not be silently shared across Python/Triton runtimes.
Capacity must be revalidated immediately before each retry because other users may legitimately acquire previously free GPUs.
limitations: Several failed attempts ended before producing candidate videos.
The successful runner fixes still require completion on real inputs before being marked WORKING.
next_actions: Complete case 2 and case 3 with the port/rank/cache-isolated runner, then evaluate raw outputs before expanding to more seeds.
